title: Day 91 · Week 13, Day 0 — Body: from building to growing — seventy-three grams to three and a half kilos, the three charts that disagree, what a percentile means, and the thirty grams of calcium
summary: Week 13: the baby is about 7.4 cm and ~73 g, sex organs complete inside, movements turning deliberate, sucking rehearsed — and the main job switches from building organs to growing. The Hadlock weight curve (73 g at 13 weeks to 3,619 g at 40: fast in proportion early, ~200 g a week late). Why crown-rump length stops at ~14 weeks, the five second-trimester measurements, and why a later scan doesn't move a well-dated due date (ACOG redating thresholds). The three charts — Hadlock 1991 (392 women), INTERGROWTH-21st standards (4,321 pregnancies, eight countries) and the WHO charts (1,387 women, ten countries; boys 3.5–4.5% larger, maternal height, age, weight and parity shift size) — and the standard-versus-reference argument. What a percentile is; fetal growth restriction (<10th percentile EFW or AC, severe <3rd, up to 10% of pregnancies, most serious before 32 weeks); constitutionally small babies; fundal height from 24 weeks with a 3 cm trigger. The skeleton: ~30 g of calcium at term, 80% in the third trimester, covered by a doubling of gut absorption; 1,000 mg/day intake; high-dose calcium halves preeclampsia only where diets are low in calcium (Cochrane 2018).
action: Find the dating scan report in the pregnancy file. On a new 'Growth' page, write the confirmed due date and the gestational age the scan gave on the day it was done; add one question for the next appointment: 'Which fetal growth chart does the clinic use?'
